note: Working draft. The difference from the published data/glossary.json, not a full copy.

data.Definition: A written history of ownership of a parcel of land, summarizing the material parts of any occurrence affecting title of said land.
Breakdown of the costs, by line item, associated with the work to be conducted in the rehabilitation of the property.

Applies to all MISMO Products (standards and collateral) issued prior to January 1, 2018. This license is automatically granted when an organization downloads any MISMO Product (MISMO standards or collateral) with an issue date through December 31, 2017.
data.Source: MISMO Governing Documents|Data Governance & Management CoP (DGM)

changeSet.Definition: Perry's Test Term 2026

Applies to all MISMO Products (standards and collateral) issued prior to January 1, 2018. This license is automatically granted when an organization downloads any MISMO Product (MISMO standards or collateral) with an issue date through December 31, 2017.

Ability to Repay (ATR) requires that a lender make a reasonable, good-faith determination before or when consummating a mortgage loan that the consumer has a reasonable ability to repay the loan, considering such factors as the consumer’s income or assets and employment status

The part of a Web page that is visible once the page has loaded — normally the top part. This term is pertinent to the electronic mortgage world as E-sign requires the presentation of documents to be compliant with state statutes that govern font, pagination, format etc.
When true, indicates that a Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) or Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) was associated with the agency.

The cyclical process of receiving principal, interest, taxes and insurance (PITI) payments from borrowers, applying the funds to a loan's financial record and ensuring that these payments are properly reported and disbursed to Investors, Insurers, Tax Agencies and others as appropriate.
The process of managing and marketing properties obtained through default on behalf of the investor or guarantor. Often an insurer will market a foreclosed property on their own behalf.
An entity that purchases mortgages from financial institutions and then securitizes them into mortgage-backed securities (MBS).

A step-by-step procedure used to solve a problem or accomplish a specific end. It is a sequence of instructions that are followed to perform a computation or solve a class of problems, often involving the repetition of operations.

changeSet.Term: Application Disclosure: Additional Credit And Debt
changeSet.Definition: A notice from the loan originator to the borrower that the borrower must notify the loan originator of any additional loan debt that the borrower takes on after loan application and before the loan closing.
A set of rules or protocols that enables software applications to communicate with each other. APIs act as intermediaries, allowing different programs to exchange data, features, and functionality.

changeSet.Term: Appraisal Review: Exterior Only Inspection With Value Opinion
changeSet.Definition: A USPAP compliant review by an appraiser in which the scope of work includes the development of a value conclusion and an exterior-only inspection of the subject property was performed in the field.

changeSet.Term: Appraisal Review: Interior Exterior Inspection With Value Opinion
changeSet.Definition: A USPAP compliant review by an appraiser in which the scope of work includes the development of a value conclusion and an interior and exterior inspection of the subject property was performed in the field.

changeSet.Term: Appraisal Review: Interior Exterior Without Value Opinion
changeSet.Definition: A USPAP compliant review by an appraiser in which the scope of work DOES NOT include the development of a value conclusion and an interior and exterior inspection of the subject property was performed in the field.

changeSet.Term: Appraisal Review: No Inspection With Value Opinion
changeSet.Definition: A USPAP compliant review by an appraiser in which the scope of work includes the development of a value conclusion however no inspection of the subject property was performed.
A USPAP compliant review by an appraiser in which the scope of work DOES NOT include the development of a value conclusion and no inspection of the subject property was performed.

The application of artificial intelligence techniques to analyze and interpret data, derive insights, and make predictions or recommendations. It involves using advanced technologies like machine learning and natural language processing to enhance decision making capabilities.
The process of analyzing credit scores to determine risk within the portfolio.

1) Process: The transfer of ownership, rights or interests in property, as in a mortgage, lease or deed of trust. Mortgages and other security instruments are regularly assigned from one investor to another and commitments by HUD/FHA to insure mortgages may be assigned by one originating lender to another before insurance. 2) Document: Transfers the beneficial interest in a instrument from one party to another.
A written agreement that a property buyer will assume responsibility for the obligations of a mortgage from the builder or original owner.
The process in which prospective borrower(s) may attend homeownership education and/or counseling.

The unique, identifiable, and unalterable copy of the Transferrable Record (eNote) maintained within the Control environment established by the Controller. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.

A valuation report from an automated valuation model or system that is not signed by a certified or licensed appraiser and contains both property data and an estimate of value usually quantified by some type of confidence score, a value definition and some level of condition of property report from a physical inspection.
A decimal value representing a fraction of one, which represents the estimated probability of an AVM value being within +/- 10% of the market value as of the AVM’s effective date.

Architecture Work Group. The AWG manages MISMO engineering disciplines providing overall technical direction and support for all MISMO Products. AWG is responsible to ensure that MISMO Products follow all published MEGs and other established product development guidelines.
The Budget and Finance Committee (BFC) primary responsibility is to manage, review and recommend to the Board the annual budget.

1) The price at which a seller will sell particular securities. In the securities and commodities trade, the highest price offered for a security or commodity at a given time. Also called a quotation or quote. 2) Describes required home repairs or improvements and provides an estimation of cost to complete. AKA: Estimate to Complete Work, Repair Estimate, Alteration Improvement and Repairs.

Under Section 6 of the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act, a written request to the loan servicer which identifies the borrower by name and account, includes a statement of reasons why the borrower believes the mortgage account is in error, and which should include the words qualified written request. The servicer has legal deadlines to respond to a qualified written request.

A report produced by a real estate sales person or broker which provides an estimation of the subject property's most probable selling price and a listing of comparable sales but with no physical inspection of the subject property.

A report produced by a real estate sales person or broker which provides an estimation of the subject property's most probable selling price and a listing of comparable sales and includes details from a physical inspection of the subject property.
Fire and extended coverage insurance for a building under construction. Coverage increases automatically as the building progresses and terminates at completion.

1)Days on which a bank or market is open for business or trading; usually excludes Saturdays, Sundays and legal public holidays. 2)The type of day used by business partners to specify time-bound requirements for processing an eMortgage.
Economic conditions in which the supply of housing exceeds demand. Sellers may be forced to make substantial price concessions.

Confirms results from the HUD Credit Alert Interactive Voice Response System, which indicates whether the individual is in default on direct or guaranteed federal loans or are otherwise ineligible for an FHA loan. Result is transcribed or captured as a screen-print from the HUD website. AKA: CAIVRS.

Development Process Document Only: 1. Failure to adhere to, or rejection of, the IPR or Antitrust Policies; 2. Repeated blatant disregard of MISMO-approved processes after receiving a written request from MISMO to cease and desist prohibited activities; and 3. Making endorsement claims prohibited of a MISMO Member (or that would be prohibited of a person or entity if they were a Member) under MISMOs Bylaws or MISMO-approved processes. Policies and Procedures Only: 1. Failure to adhere to or rejection of the IPR or Antitrust Policies. 2. Repeated blatant disregard of these Policies and Procedures after receiving a written request from MISMO to cease and desist prohibited activities; and 3. Making endorsement claims prohibited of a MISMO Member (or that would be prohibited of a person or entity if they were a Member) under MISMOs Bylaws or these Policies and Procedures.

A trusted third-party organization or company that issues, manages, renews, and revokes Digital Certificates used to create Digital Signatures. The Certificate Authority registers the certificate holder's name and address and allows others to see if the certificate is valid, revoked, or expired. The third-party certificate authority also has the ability to confirm the identity of the certificate holder. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.

Public Key Infrastructure term. A list of Digital Certificates that are revoked. CRLs are an important part of Public Key Infrastructure, as they validate that the certificate used by the Digital Signature on an Electronic Record has not been revoked and may be trusted. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.

A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the reason for the changed circumstance altering information on the Loan Estimate or Closing Disclosure. As defined in Regulation Z, an extraordinary or unexpected event beyond control of any interested party, or any new information which affects the consumer or loan transaction, thereby changing information that the creditor relied upon when providing the Loan Estimate.
Development Process Document Only: A brief statement describing a WG's purpose and scope Policies and Procedures Only: See Work Group Charter
Represents money payable or paid (if cancelled). AKA: Checks, Cancelled Checks.
Describes the legal obligation of a parent to pay money toward the care and maintenance of his/her children.

As of fiscal year 2008, all agencies are required to utilize an automated counseling application of their choice. The application is generally referred to as the “Client Management System”. The purpose of the system is to automate counseling services, store client data, and interface with the Housing Counseling System's Agency Reporting Module to submit required data to HUD.
Requests that a line of credit be closed after receiving a payoff under a separate cover. AKA: account Closure Letter.

Closing Disclosure using the alternative disclosures and modifications permitted for transactions without a seller. Refers to Exhibit H 25(J) "Modification to Closing Disclosure for Transaction Not Involving Seller" in the CFPB Integrated Mortgage Disclosures Regulation.
For split disclosures, the borrower-only representation.

Closing Disclosure providing both borrower and seller sides of the real estate transaction. Refers to Exhibit H 25(A) "Mortgage Loan Transaction Closing Disclosure Model Form" in the CFPB Integrated Mortgage Disclosures Regulation.
For split disclosures, the property seller-only representation.
Council of Chairs. The CoC serves as a forum for all MISMO WGs to communicate and exchange information on topics of general and shared interest across all WGs.
Process of reconciling the loan fees with the Settlement Agent to ensure accuracy of the final Closing Disclosure (CD).

Process of collecting and confirming data both internally and with third parties that will be used to produce a Closing Disclosure (CD) for the Borrower and the Uniform Closing Dataset (UCD) for GSE delivery.
Focused on real estate finance transactions related to the origination, sale, and servicing of multifamily dwellings, office buildings, and other non-residential development projects.
Community of Practice. A COP represents the business or technology interests of an industry segment and is made up of subject matter experts for that particular segment of the industry.

The lender uses a comparative income analysis document to compare the performance of a self-employed borrower's business over a period of years to determine its viability. Fannie Mae Form 1088 July 96.

Establishes that the borrower will accommodate changes to loan documentation that result from errors and omissions, to ensure that the documents conform to industry standards. AKA: Errors and Omissions, E & O.

Documentation or information that must exist (""be satisfied"") at or before a point in the origination process, such as Prior to Closing, Prior to Funding, etc. Common conditions include proof of mortgage insurance (when applicable), proof of homeowners insurance, and requests for additional documentation.
Confirms the percentage of a Condominium (Condo) Association or phase is currently occupied.

Data and information assets must be confined to authorized access and not be disclosed to others who do not have a need to know. Exact criteria for criticality is to be determined by each organization
Authorizes a person to sign documents for a borrower.
Describes Adjustable Rate Mortgages and reviews their benefits and risks. AKA: CHARM.

A Participant has control of a Transferable Record if a system employed for evidencing the transfer of interests in the Transferable Record reliably establishes that Participant as the Participant to which the Transferable Record was issued or transferred pursuant to Section 16 of UETA and Section 201 of E-SIGN. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org

The Party (entity) named on the System of Record that has Control of the eNote. For example, the Controller can be thought of as the "holder," "holder in due course," and/or "purchaser" of an original paper note as defined under the Uniform Commercial Code. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.

The Controller Delegatee for Transfer Model is used to allow one party to submit registration and transfers on behalf of another party on the MERS eRegistry. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.
A document that notifies the borrower of upcoming conversion options and scheduled interest rate changes..
Transfers title to a property from a seller (grantor) to a recipient (grantee); provides evidence of the legal right of ownership.
Contains data about the property sale and conveyance tax calculations. Accompanies a Conveyance Deed at the time of recording. AKA: Deed Tax Form; Conveyance Tax Return.
Establishes the rules for governing and operating the Cooperative (Coop) Housing Corporation.
Establishes the responsibility of the Cooperative (Coop) to notify the lender in the event of borrower default.

The process of removing a loan from the records of a investor - sometimes a loan is reclassified from a pool or security ahead of foreclosure and being fully removed from the Investor's books. Some portion of interim Investor accounting changes may have occurred earlier in the default management process based on the servicing agreement.
Community of Practice. A COP represents the business or technology interests of an industry segment and is made up of subject matter experts for that particular segment of the industry.
Informs a cosigner of a loan that they will be obligated to pay the debt if there is a default by the main borrowers on the loan.
Confirms that the borrower has completed counseling related to their mortgage and property obligations
Provides proof to lenders and other interested parties that clients have completed home retention counseling from a HUD-approved counseling agency. AKA: HUD-9912.
Informs the borrower of certain Veterans' Affairs items of interest regarding the loan and financing eligibility. AKA: VA 26-0592.
The process of sending billing statements, payment schedules or payment coupons.
Financial status — ability of borrowers to meet the terms of their obligations.

1) A report run by an independent credit agency which verifies certain information concerning an applicant’s credit standing 2) Describes the borrowers credit history. Provided by a credit reporting bureau, or a service which consolidates reports from multiple sources into a single report (Tri-merge). AKA: Tri-Merge, Residential Mortgage Credit Report (RMCR).
Data element where erroneous or unavailable data would cause negative consequences to the organization. Exact criteria for criticality is to be determined by each organization.

The Residential Standards Governance Committee and the Commercial Standards Governance Committee work in concert with the MISMO Officers and the MISMO Manager and other MISMO committees and report to the MISMO Board of Directors.

Verifies the identity of any person seeking to open an account; maintains records of the information used to verify the person's identity; and determines whether the person appears on any lists of known or suspected terrorists. AKA: U.S. Patriot Act, Important Applicant Information.
The timely and reliable access to and use of information or information systems.

A systematic error that causes a deviation from the expected or true values in the data. It can lead to an inaccurate or unfair representation of reality and often stems from two main sources: 1)Data: Bias can arise from the way data is collected, processed, or used. For example, if a dataset is not representative of the population it’s meant to reflect, it can introduce bias into the analysis 2)Human Element: Bias can also come from the individuals who collect, analyze, or interpret the data. Personal beliefs, assumptions, or errors can inadvertently affect the outcomes of data-driven processes
An atomic unit of data that has precise meaning or precise semantics.
A record of the data life cycle that includes the data's origins and where it moves over time.
The degree to which data is fit for a given business process or operation.
Confirms the date, location and cause of the death of a person. Issued by a government official.
A free-form text field capturing explanations to a “yes” answer to any declaration on the loan application.

A Member of the MERS eRegistry that is authorized by the Controller to perform certain MERS eRegistry transactions on the Controller's behalf. The DT can initiate registrations and transfers of Control, but may not initiate change status transactions, or change data transactions except to remove themselves as DT. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.
Process of delivering an accurate Closing Disclosure (CD) to the Borrower via mail, electronically, or in person.
Process of securely delivering the closing documents package electronically, or as an exception in paper, to the Settlement Agent.
The study of the characteristics of human populations such as size, growth, density, distribution and vital statistics. Also known as demographics.
The process of deriving the data needed for the HMDA Loan Application Register (LAR).

changeSet.Term: Determine Lien Position and Relative Ownership
changeSet.Definition: The process of determining the loan's lien position regarding the property. This may be performed multiple times within the Default Management process.

1) Development Process Document Only: The formal process, described in detail in this document, by which MISMO develops, tests, approves, and publishes its MISMO Products. 2) Policies and Procedures Only: The formal process, described in detail in the Development Process document, by which MISMO develops, tests, approves, and publishes its MISMO Products. 3) MBA Glossary: The process through which development projects are conceived, initiated, analyzed, financed, designed, built and managed.
Non Personally Identifiable Data used for research or under evaluation for use in the organization.
Establishes the terms of the divorce. Provided by a court or legal authority. AKA: Final Judgment (divorce), Abridgment of Judgment (divorce).
Confirms that an appraisal report has been delivered, describes how delivered, to whom and when.

A Document Profile is a concept developed by the MISMO eMortgage Workgroup to distinguish features and characteristics of the Version 3 SMART Doc. The four profiles accommodate different usage scenarios. Each profile includes and extends the previous one. 1. Basic: The document receiver only needs the view, information related to signatures if the document is signed and the document type or name. 2. Retrievable: The document receiver wants to access data from the document and there is not a requirement to automatically verify that the data matches what is presented in the viewable image. The data in the Retrievable profile may or may not include all of the information contained in the view. 3. Tamper Evident: The document receiver wants to verify the integrity of the document. 4. Verifiable: The document receiver wants to verify that the data matches the information contained in the view.

A document that expresses the sequence in which documents occur within a document set. The investor often dictates the document sequence to simplify document processing. A document set sometimes includes the DocumentSequence document itself. AKA: Documentation Order, Stacking Sheet.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies a borrower’s relationship with an individual who is not a legal spouse but who has real property rights similar to those of a legal spouse.

Document Type Definition. A file that defines the "markup language" that will be used to describe the data. It defines and names the elements that can be used in the document, the order in which the elements can appear, the element attributes that can be used, and other document features. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.
Development Work Group. A DWG produces a MISMO Product, or set of Products, as specified in its Charter.

Information within a notarized electronic record that confirms the notary public's name, jurisdiction, identifying number, and commission expiration date and generally corresponds to information in notary seals used on paper documents.
A document issued by an employer which evidences a person's identity and employee identifier.

An individual or organization who makes, has made, uses, distributes, imports, modifies, reproduces, publishes, displays, or makes derivative works using, or that are compliant with, a MISMO Product where the individual or organization uses the MISMO Product (including derivative and compliant works) either (a) for its own internal business purposes, or (b) within the confines of its organization without distribution to any third party.
A report rendered by an engineer stating the physical condition of property that has been inspected, with a summation or recommendation thereof.
Any notarial act performed electronically, that a notarial officer may perform under state law.

The process of creating the initial record in the MERS eRegistry for identifying the Controller, Location, and other key information of the eNote. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual as "eNote Registration Record" and is available at members.mersinc.org.

1) The act of registering the security instrument electronically with the county recorder or similar jurisdictional authority. 2) An act of registering the security instrument and other recordable documents electronically with the county recorder or similar jurisdictional authority. eRecording does not require the security instrument to be electronically executed. A county often records a scanned image of the paper security instrument when it eRecords. For models of eRecording, see the PRIA Technology Committee Business Requirements Work Group: Models of eRecording - A Continuum of eRecording - https://www.pria.us/i4a/doclibrary

An annual review and recalculation of the escrow account based on actual amounts paid into the escrow account and actual amounts disbursed from the escrow account as required by RESPA. The actual amounts are compared to the projected amounts from the prior year's disclosure.
Confirms work on the property has been completed and any funds held in escrow can be released. AKA: Work Escrow Mortgagee Assurance of Completion (2300).

Confirms the lender agrees to waive collecting a monthly payment for taxes and insurance (escrow or impound account). Informs the applicant of their responsibilities to pay tax/insurance bills when due, whether an escrow waiver fee will be imposed, and information regarding lender placement of insurance. AKA: Notice Regarding Payments For Homeowners Insurance And Property Taxes, Escrow Account Notice.
Establish a plan to cure a short term delinquency by temporarily increasing the amount or frequency of the payment without changing the terms of the loan.
A type of valuation report produced by an appropriately qualified, competent and independent person.

A report produced by an appropriately qualified, competent and independent person and includes the development of a value conclusion without a physical inspection and may rely on expert systems and data.

A report produced by an appropriately qualified, competent and independent person and includes the development of a value conclusion and includes an exterior inspection of the property and may also rely on expert systems and data.
The process of transferring serviced loan(s) from one Servicer to another.

Informs the borrower that it is illegal to discriminate in lending practices. This is different that the Equal Credit Opportunity Act. AKA: The Housing Financial Discrimination Act of 1977 Fair Lending Notice.

The nation's largest mortgage investor, created in 1968 by an amendment to Title III of the National Housing Act (12 USC 1716 et seq.). This stockholder-owned corporation, a portion of whose board of directors is appointed by the President of the United States, supports the secondary market in mortgages on residential property with mortgage purchase and securitization programs. aka Federal National Mortgage Association (FNMA).

changeSet.Term: Federal Information Processing Standard (140-2) or FIPS (140-2)
changeSet.Definition: Federal Information Processing Standard (140-2), which specifies the security requirements that will be satisfied by a cryptographic module, providing four increasing, qualitative levels intended to cover a wide range of potential applications and environments.
See Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. Commonly referred to as the Fed.

changeSet.Term: FHA Limited Denial Of Participation General Services Administration Checklist
changeSet.Definition: Confirms that a borrower is not recorded on the LDP/GSA (Limited Denial of Participation/General Services Administration) lists, and therefore is eligible for an FHA loan.
Determines the appropriate amount for an FHA loan. AKA: MCAW.
See REFERRAL.
Establishes that a borrower will maintain flood insurance in the amount prescribed by the lender for the duration of the loan term.

An agreement between a servicer and a borrower in which the servicer agrees to a temporary reduction or suspension of the mortgage payments. At the end of the period, the borrower is expected to repay the suspended amount based on agreed terms and resume normal payment. A forbearance plan is usually occurs when a borrower experiences a temporary, significant loss of income.

A notice from the servicer to the borrower regarding the intention or status of placing a homeowner's insurance policy on the borrower's property in order to protect the servicer's investment. The servicer has been notified of lapsed or insufficient insurance coverage. May include any required supplemental insurance policies.
Notice to the borrower that the servicer has cancelled the homeowner's insurance it force placed on the property at the borrower's expense. The letter may Include premium refund terms.

The servicer's initial notice to the borrower of the intent to force place homeowner's insurance on the property unless evidence of an active acceptable policy is provided. AKA: Initial Notice of Intent To Force Placed Insurance

changeSet.Term: Force Placed Insurance Notice: Insufficient Documentation
changeSet.Definition: The servicer's second and final notice to the borrower of the intent to force place homeowner's insurance on the property unless evidence of an active acceptable policy is provided. The borrower has provided insufficient documentation in response to the Initial Notice of Intent To Force Placed Insurance. AKA: Second And Final Response For Insufficient Documentation
Notice to the borrower that the servicer has placed homeowner's insurance on the property at the borrower's expense.

ForcePlacedInsuranceNotice:Renewal : Notice to the borrower that the servicer will renew force placed homeowner's insurance unless the borrower provides evidence that they have secured an alternate acceptable policy.

Created by Congress in Title III of the Emergency Home Finance Act of 1970 (12 USC 1451 et seq.). This stockholder-owned corporation, a portion of whose board of directors is appointed by the President of the United States, supports the secondary market in mortgages on residential and multifamily properties with mortgage purchase and securitization programs. aka Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (FHLMC).
Federal Reserve System
Confirms final closing information and numbers on a brokered or third party closing. AKA: Funding Worksheet.

Confirms receipt of all the disclosures in the Disclosure Booklet, HUD Guide to Settlement Costs. Also used to document the float/lock rate requests and mortgage insurance requests and provide the Appraisal Notice to the borrower. AKA: GLAD.
Process of producing the unsigned closing documents package that satisfies the terms of the loan underwriting approval.
The process of generating disbursement documentation which includes the ALTA Settlement Statement or Closing Statement, and the Seller/Borrower Disbursement Authorizations.

1)A document which tells borrowers the approximate costs they will pay at or before settlement, based on common practice in the locality. Under requirements of the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act (RESPA), the mortgage banker or mortgage broker, if any, must deliver or mail the GFE to the applicant within three business days after the application is received. 2)Describes the approximate costs borrower will pay at or before settlement, based on common practice in the locality. The mortgage banker or mortgage broker, if any, must deliver or mail the GFE to the applicant within three business days after the application is received. This document is a part of HUD Regulation X (RESPA/Reg X). AKA: Good Faith Estimate.

The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, otherwise known as the Financial Modernization Act of 1999, requires companies to give consumers privacy notices that explain the institutions’ information-sharing practices. In turn, consumers have the right to limit some — but not all — sharing of their information.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the adult member of the family who is identified for purposes of determining eligibility for social services and counseling.
Informs the borrower that the costs associated with the new HECM loan will not exceed the loan amount.
Evidence, often a screen print, of calculation for HECM principal limit and monthly payment amount.
A worksheet that provides the required information on credit history, income and expenses, and the calculation of residual income is captured. Lenders may use the HUD HECM Financial Assessment
Describes final loan information and figures in a HECM transaction.
Describes the charges associated with the HECM loan and the payments made to the borrower.
Determines whether the loan is high cost or predatory based on state or national statutes. AKA: Anti-Predatory Worksheet.
Agrees to hold harmless and indemnify (assumes the legal liability of) the lender from any future liability on items defined in the notice. AKA: Indemnity Notice.
Confirms that the borrower has completed a homebuyer education program. The programs are usually in association with first time homebuyer and affordable housing programs.
Authorizes lender to freeze a Home Equity Line of Credit in anticipation of a pay off.

One of Fannie Mae’s major tools for neighborhood and community revitalization, the HomeStyle Second Mortgage is designed for home-buyers or homeowners at all income levels who wish to repair, remodel, enlarge or substantially renovate a home. Introduced in 1993, this program was designed to help lenders capture the growing U.S. market for home remodeling.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the setting in which the borrower received counseling or homeownership education.

The HUD-9902, known as the Housing Counseling Activity Report, is a tool HUD uses to track the Housing Counseling Program. HUD-9902 Housing Counseling Agency Activity Reports are cumulative fiscal year-to-date for each quarterly report period. The data collected helps demonstrate the program“s impact to Congress and other industry stakeholders. The form is designed to capture all of a HUD-approved Housing Counseling Agency's education and counseling activities within HUD”s fiscal year. Marketing and outreach activities, such as fliers mailed or calls made, should not be recorded. The HUD-9902 also captures a client’s demographic characteristics, income level, counseling type, and counseling outcomes.

Housing Counseling System is a real-time web application that manages the counseling program data. It maintains the list of agencies, collects client data, processes grant applications, and provides performance reports.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the lender's approval status as a mortgagee of the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that is used to identify how the Housing Counseling Applicant learned about the Housing Counseling Agency.
Used to verify the identities of those using electronic signatures.

An identity proofing method that relies on something you know - the verification of information that is unique to the Principal, should be known by the Principal, and can be readily demonstrated by the Principal. Some common forms of this type of identity proofing include Knowledge- Based Authentication (KBA), passwords, or personal identification numbers. See also definition of Knowledge-Based Authentication

An identity proofing method that relies on the verification of something you are - the Principal's unique personal traits. Some common forms of this type of identity proofing include comparisons of fingerprints, iris, voice, or face to a reference scan.

An identity proofing method that relies on something you have - the verification of the Principal's possession of unique information or credentials. Some common forms of this type of identity proofing include Digital Certificates, physical or digital government-issued identification cards, one-time passwords, or a response to a message delivered to a mobile device.

Information Management Work Group. IM ensures that consistent business definitions and business information are used across MISMO Products including but not limited to the Business Glossary, Business Reference Model including MISMO Life of Loan, Logical Data Model and related platform dependent models as applicable, and MISMO XML Reference Model and the supporting Collateral. IM is responsible for ensuring that MISMO Products follow all published MEGs and other established product development guidelines.
A notarial act in which documents are notarized in electronic form in the physical presence of the notary.

The practice of identifying the sensitivity of information considering the risk and impact of the information being accessed, disclosed, modified, used or destroyed without proper authorization and the potential harm resulting from such unauthorized access, disclosure, modification, use or destruction.
Initial disclosure of potential rate or payment change per CFPB regulation.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the intended use of a credit report in alignment with the Fair Credit Reporting Act section 604(Permissible Purposes of a Consumer Credit Report).

changeSet.Term: Interest Rate And Discount Disclosure Statement
changeSet.Definition: Discloses the interest rate and discount points to the borrower and are an agreement between the borrower and the lender. The Veteran's Affairs does not govern the rate or points on the loan. AKA: Interest Rate and Discount Disclosure.
Programs that subsidize the market interest rate on mortgage loans, thus lowering the consumer’s housing cost.
A numerical label assigned to each device connected to a computer network that uses the internet protocol for communication
Provides bill which itemizes nature and cost of transactions. AKA: Bill.
U.S. Income Tax Return for Estates and Trusts.
Acquisition or Abandonment of Secured Property
Proceeds From Broker and Barter Exchange Transactions
Cancellation of Debt
Changes in Corporate Control and Capital Structure
Dividends and Distributions
Payments From Qualified Education Programs (Under Sections 529 and 530)
Distributions From Pensions, Annuities, Retirement or Profit-Sharing Plans, IRAs, Insurance Contracts, etc.
Proceeds From Real Estate Transactions
Distributions From an HSA, Archer MSA, or Medicare Advantage MSA
U.S. Corporation Income Tax Return.
U.S. Income Tax Return for an S Corporation.
Identifies a Tax Transcript from the IRS.
Confirms a person's wage income and taxes withheld. AKA: Wage and Tax Statement.
Confirms the individual is a foreign tax resident. AKA: IRS Certificate of Foreign Status.
Describes the finance charges associated with the mortgage loan. May be included in the TIL Disclosure document.

1) A formal decision given by a court or an obligation (such as a debt) created by the decree and/or a certificate evidencing such a decree. 2) Final determination by a court of the rights and claims of the parties to an action.
Establishes the interest in land of a person who owns the lease granted by the property owner.
Establishes the rights of others over an individual's (the Testator's) property after the individual's death. AKA: Certificate of Appointment, Letters of Testamentary.

1)The period during which a property owner is actively leasing vacant units or square feet to tenants in an effort to stabilize the property. The process of leasing up. 2)Fully occupied or almost fully occupied; enough commercial space within a property is rented to tenants under lease agreements that the property has stabilized (leased-up).

A property description, recognized by law, that is sufficient to locate and identify the property without oral testimony. This is primarily a component of other documents (i.e. security instruments, title policies, commitments), but is received separately on some occasions.
Specifies agreement between a company and an individual to pay a pre-determined amount of money to a beneficiary if the insured dies during the policy term.
Describes in detail the budget for the construction of a home.

Provides information about the employment, income, assets, debts and other financial information of the prospective borrowers. Includes information about the purpose of the home loan and about the property securing the home loan. Provided by Borrower with assistance from the lender. AKA: Uniform Residential Loan Application, 1003, Credit Application, 65.
Residential Loan Application for Reverse Mortgages
Uniform Residential Loan Application
Informs the borrower of total finance charges and interest rates associated with the loan.

When true, indicates the Borrower answered “yes” to the declaration question: “Have you directly or indirectly been obligated on any loan that resulted in foreclosure, transfer of title in lieu of foreclosure, or judgment?”

changeSet.Term: Loan Modification Trial Payment Period Agreement
changeSet.Definition: An agreement between a servicer and a borrower to temporarily modify the terms of a mortgage loan for a trial payment period (TPP) and either modify existing or establish new conditions as appropriate.
Provides Lender with information to determine the amount required to pay off an account and the outstanding principle balance as of a specific date.
Describes transactions recorded and account balances of a customers accounts during a specified period.

To document the XML Reference Model, MISMO creates a Logical Data Dictionary (LDD) that defines each XML data element used for electronic transactions. The result is a single, common data set for the mortgage industry. The borrower, employment, property and other commonly used information have a common data definition, no matter which mortgage industry segment is using the data. A catalog of key components of the MISMO Reference Model, including terms, containers, data attributes, and ARCROLES.

The Logical Data Model (LDM) will make it easier for organizations to communicate regardless of the technologies they choose to use for communicating with business partners. The LDM will support XML and JSON, which is the technology of choice for mobile transactions. The LDM was built using Unified Modeling Language (UML) 2.5, a common standard created by the Object Management Group. UML consists of an integrated set of diagrams that helps users specify, visualize, construct and document software or business systems. MISMO has also created a set of user guidelines to help industry participants adopt and implement the LDM in their business processes.

The process of creating, maintaining documentation evidencing the servicer's response to a qualified written request (QWR) from a consumer. The QWR is a request for action or information as outlined in the National Servicing Rules and supplemental guidance from the CFPB or other regulator(s). Per the National Servicing Rules, a servicer must be able to communicate their compliance actions to regulators, transferees or interested third parties when requested.

The process of extending and recovering advances for Property Taxes, Hazard Insurance, HOA dues, Leasehold payments and Property Preservation expenses. Some of these processes are part of the Escrow Management function however they may also be a part of default management.

The process of managing all activities related to non-performing loans. These activities maybe driven by the borrower willingness to participate, loan documents, investor regulations, servicer requirements and state and federal regulations.

The process of establishing and managing any required trust accounts where funds are allocated for payment of taxes, insurance and other items as they become due. In addition, the process of tracking the status of tax and insurance payments on non-escrowed loans.
The process of tracking damage notifications, repairs, disaster declaration driven claims, management of insurance proceeds and the interaction between insurance companies and borrowers.

The process of assigning and managing loans made under alternative loan programs and products such as state bond programs, ARMs, HELOCs, Buydowns or loans made to an acknowledged VIP. Includes compliance with Servicemember's Civil Relief Act (SCRA).
The process of identifying, evaluating and quantifying risks followed by coordinated and economical application of resources to minimize, monitor and control the probability or impact of that risk.
The process of removing MI coverage based upon investor guidelines. This may be automatic or upon the request of the borrower and includes appropriate notifications.
Proves the ownership of the manufactured home and shows any liens on the property. Lists the manufacturer, serial numbers, and date of manufacture.
A signed certification, verifying the truth and accuracy of the information with respect to marital status.
Confirms that a marriage has occurred.

A MISMO Engineering Guideline (MEG) is published to assist the work groups in creating their specifications and to assist developers of MISMO Products to achieve consistent and technically appropriate products that meet the needs of the user community. The MEGs shall be adhered to during the development process without any deviation. MISMO has developed a series of MEGs to guide the process and production of Version 3.x Reference Model. In the event of a conflict between the MEGs and the DPD, the DPD takes precedence.

A secure method for distributing eMortgage packages from one MERS eRegistry Member to another, using the existing MERS eRegistry infrastructure and transaction security requirements. This term is defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.

The mortgage insurance application provides information about a prospective borrower, the loan program, AU decision, MI premium plan, etc. The MI Application is generally sent by the lender along with the corresponding GSE form 1003/65 and/or GSE 1008/1077.
Establishes a commitment to issue mortgage insurance pending specified conditions.
Notice issued to the lender to indicate a mortgage insurance underwriting decision of declined.
Changes one or more of the terms of the Mortgage Insurance Certificate after closing.
Confirms that a person served in the military and describes their veterans status. AKA: DD Form 214, DD214.
A dedicated MISMO staff resource to ensure all work products are developed in a timely and consistent manner. The Program Manager will track status and progress of all work products.

Monitoring bankruptcy activities and performing administrative tasks on behalf of the trustee, borrower or legal entities associated with the bankruptcy. Bankruptcy processes are fairly standard and driven by federal regulations and the Chapter filed.
The Monthly Summary of Assistance Payments document is due under HUD Sections 235(b), 235(i), or 235(j), or of Interest Reduction Payments due under Section 236. HUD-300 (04/2003).

A MISMO dataset that contains the loan data fields and delivery file format that lenders must provide regulators for the origination loan portfolio review portion of regulatory compliance examinations. In addition, the data standard to perform pre-closing, post-closing, secondary market, and regulatory compliance audits.

A method of access control in which a user is granted access after successfully presenting evidence through a minimum of two methods of authentication of identity verification. See also, Identity Verification by Knowledge, Identity Verification by Possession, and Identity Verification by Personal Trait.

The National Housing Resource Center is dedicated to organizing nonprofit housing counseling agencies into a unified voice to advocate for the housing counseling industry and on behalf of housing consumers.
A national identity document used in many countries in Central and South America. Evidences a person's identity and national Identifier.
The Nominating Committees (NC)'s primary responsibility is to identify and develop future board members and leaders.
Identifies the nearest living relative of the borrower.

A signed certification obtained at loan closing from the Non-Borrowing Spouse, verifying the truth and accuracy of the information provided in the application with respect to the Non-Borrowing Spouse's marital status, and occupancy status of the principal residence.

changeSet.Term: Non Borrowing Spouse Certification Letter: Eligible
changeSet.Definition: A signed certification obtained from the Non-Borrowing Spouse which meets the current guidelines of the loan program. For HECM loans, this would mean that the Non-Borrowing Spouse is not married to the borrower, or does not occupy the property as their primary residence. In the event the last surviving borrower passes away before an eligible non-borrowing spouse, the due and payable status will be deferred.
When true, indicates that housing counseling fee is offset by funding from a grant source other than HUD.

Any individual who engages in one or more MISMO Development Work Group (DWG) or other activities that is not a MISMO Member or an employee of an organization that has a MISMO membership in good standing. Such activities include, but are not limited to making a Contribution, attending meetings, or participating by telephone, Internet, or e-mail. All Non- Members are "Participants" under the terms of the IPR Policy.
An individual who signs records during a remote online notarization but is not the Principal to the transaction. See also Principal Signer.

1) A general term for any kind of paper or document signed by a borrower that is an acknowledgment of the debt and is, by inference, a promise to pay. When the note is secured by a mortgage, it is called a mortgage note and the mortgagee is named as the payee. 2) Establishes a legal obligation of the borrower to repay the debt. AKA: Promissory Note, Mortgage Note, Loan Agreement.
Adds the specific terms of the ARM to the promissory note.
Adds additional page(s) to the Note for endorsements.
Adds additional terms to the promissory note.

Informs the borrower of denial or other material change in the loan application. AKA: Denial Letter, Statement of Credit Denial, Termination, or Change, Notice of Adverse Action, Notice of Counter Offer, Credit Denial Letter, Withdrawal Letter, Request for More Information.
Changes (updates) a previous appraisal that was prepared subject to completion of repairs or incomplete items. AKA: FNMA 442.

1) A public notice filed with a court stating that a mortgage borrower is behind in payment. AKA: NOD 2) The notice sent to defaulting borrowers, required by insurers or guarantors such as FHA, VA or MIC.
Describes repair conditions on the subject property. Provided by Appraiser to the lender. Provided as an addendum to Appraisal. AKA: VC sheet, VC condition, valuation condition sheet.
Process of securing interim, short-term funds from the Lender's line-of-credit (Warehouse Line) established with a Warehouse Bank to fund the loan closing.
Process of obtaining a Flood Certificate which indicates whether the subject property is in a flood zone.
Process of obtaining detailed information from external resources to verify loan data during the loan origination process.
Process of engaging external resources to obtain and/or verify loan data during the loan origination process.

Policies and Procedures. This document has been adopted by the MISMO Board of Directors (aka Board) to govern the activities of the organization. The Policies and Procedures (P&Ps) defined in this document address all activities of the organization. The detailed procedures for the development of the MISMO Products are defined in separate documents.

The payoff amount of any existing Property Assessed Clean Energy (PACE) loans. These loans are made by localities to finance residential energy-related improvements and are generally repaid through the homeowner’s real estate tax bill.
Remote online notarization of paper documents (delivered via mail, courier, etc.) with use of multi-factor authentication.
Releases a specific parcel of real property from an existing security instrument.
A contract that establishes the terms of a business association between two or more entities, including the rights and responsibilities of each entity.
A document issued by a national government which certifies a person's identity, nationality, and passport identifier.

Patent Rights are all patents and patent applications owned by a MISMO License Participant that would be infringed on by an organization that makes, has made, uses, sells, offers for sale, or imports a product or service using or complying with a MISMO Standard (except for any patents and patent applications that the MISMO License Participant disclosed to MISMO as not being subject to the Royalty-Free License.) NOTE: If the patent application is unpublished, the MISMO License Participant must identify the portions of the relevant MISMO Standard that infringes on the application.
Describes income for a particular pay period.
Describes history of payments on a loan. AKA: Loan History.
Confirms the remaining principle balance of a loan that is being paid off or refinanced, based on a defined close or pay date. AKA: Demand, Demand Statement.

The Prioritization Committee (PC) is responsible for providing guidance on organizational priorities and key initiatives. This includes overseeing the Business Executive Team; Senior Advisors; and the New Product Incubator. It further includes recommending to the MISMO Board of Directors which products should be MISMO Standards and which should be MISMO Collateral.

An ISO standard for the long-term preservation of documents. In PDF/A-1: All fonts must be embedded, all color spaces must be device-independent, Javascript, embedded files, encryption, external content references, transparency, layers, and XFA forms data are prohibited, and standards-based metadata must be used.

The process of handling the assumption of an existing loan by a new party. The servicer and/or investor underwrites and approves the assumption. The servicer retains information on the original borrower and adjusts the loan information to reflect the new borrower.

The process of writing off a full or partial loan balance that is unlikely to be collected. This is an accounting event where the creditor/investor no longer considers the amount owed as a source of profit but rather counts it as a loss.

Process of completing various functions related to performing a closing; including but not limited to gathering additional requirements as specified in the approval, generating and delivering the closing package to the Settlement Agent, and execution of the closing documents by the Borrower(s).
The process of generating and executing documents to secure the loan collateral, and disbursing the proceeds.

The process of collateral reconciliation must be performed on a monthly basis for certain MBS portfolios. This is the reconciliation of the normalized actual principal balance to the scheduled principal balance. If there is a discrepancy, the loan or pool is either overcollateralized, or undercollateralized. An undercollateralization must be resolved immediately. An overcollateralization must be resolved as soon as possible, using unscheduled principal collections.

The process of using debt collection activities in an attempt to bring a non-performing loan current, which includes establishing a QRPC contact with the borrower(s). QRPC is a uniform standard for communicating with the borrower, co-borrower, or a trusted advisor (collectively referred to as "borrower") about resolution of the mortgage loan delinquency. The servicer must make every attempt to achieve QRPC. The collections process may include short term repayment plans if conditions warrant.
The process of customer relationship management (CRM) between a servicer and borrower(s) including notifications, customer service, collections and statements.

The process of transferring ownership of a property from the borrower to the servicer or investor to prevent foreclosure. If the Deed in Lieu is deemed a taxable event, this process includes reporting to both the Borrower and the IRS.

The process of removing a loan from the records of a servicer and investor by applying funds received as a result of a liquidation event. Includes ensuring that any appropriate third party notifications are made. In addition, the property may move into REO Administration.

Process of delivering recordable documents to the appropriate government agency (typically the County Recorder or County Clerk) in an electronic format so that they become part of the public land records system.

The process of taking the legal steps necessary to liquidate the loan and extinguish the debt. Federal and State regulations dictate this process. In addition, if HUD insured the loan, HUD guidance for Claims Without Conveyance of Title (CWCOT) may apply. State regulations vary substantially and it is common practice to utilize third party legal counsel where the property is located. Loss Mitigation efforts and Bankruptcy filings could have an impact on the timing of the foreclosure efforts.
Process of validating that closing has occurred, all closing conditions have been met, the wire amount is confirmed, and the disbursement of funds via wire transfer has been performed.
The process in which prospective borrower(s) may attend homeownership education and/or counseling.
The process of verifying those items which are required to be escrowed per the terms of the note or the investor. In addition, HOA and Leasehold requirements are determined and set up for monitoring.
The process of reporting non-performing loan activities according to the terms of the servicing agreement. Non-performing loan activities are spelled out in the Default Management processes.
The process of remitting funds and reporting loan activities to investors according to the terms of the servicing agreement.

The process in which a servicer and/or investor works with a delinquent borrower to determine an alternative to foreclosure. This may be a liquidation or retention workout. Arriving at the solution is largely governed by the mortgage documents and/or investor rules. Federal and State regulations drive the timing of many default management efforts. Servicers are not permitted to move forward on a foreclosure if other loss mitigation efforts are underway.
Process of completing underwriting analysis, including credit and collateral, outside of an automated system.
The process of reporting non-performing loan activities according to the MI contract. Non-performing loan activities are spelled out in the Default Management processes.
The process of reconciling loans in a servicer's portfolio with the associated mortgage insurer.
The process of verifying that the loan origination data was loaded accurately to the servicing system.
The process of conveying the property to a third party buyer, back to the borrower or into REO administration.

The process of securing and monitoring real estate acquired by a lender or investor which includes physical maintenance as well as any financial obligations to maintain the lien position on the property. This may include periodic claims for expense reimbursement of allowable maintenance costs.
The process of tracking and paying escrowed items and other required items.

The process of allowing a borrower to sell a property to a third party where the owner of the beneficial rights agrees to accept less than the amount owed to pay off the loan. The difference between the amount owed and the short sale amount may be a reportable tax event for the borrower.
Process of delivering recordable documents to the appropriate government agency (typically the County Recorder or County Clerk) so that they become part of the public land records system.

changeSet.Term: Perform Verbal VOE or Verify in File
changeSet.Definition: Process of completing a verbal, or reviewing a written, verification of employment.
The process of reviewing a loan to determine need for placement of appropriate payment application stops based on default status. Funds received are typically applied to a suspense account.

This document has been adopted by the MISMO Board of Directors (aka Board) to govern the activities of the organization. The Policies and Procedures (P&Ps) defined in this document address all activities of the organization. The detailed procedures for the development of the MISMO Products are defined in separate documents. AKA: P&Ps.
Process of evaluating the financial status of potential Borrower(s) to determine the amount and type of mortgage that may be available to the Borrower(s).
Process in which the Lender presents financing options to the prospective Borrower.
An annual explanation of the current terms of the MI which may include a Loan To Value calculation and eligibility criteria for MI cancellation per RESPA regulations.

Public Key Infrastructure term. The secret key of the Key Pair that is controlled only by the person or entity to which it was issued. By encrypting a message with the Public Key, only the holder of the Private Key can decrypt the message. Likewise, the holder of the Private key can encrypt messages that can only be decrypted by the Public key.
The process of making a claim to an investor or insurer to recover advances made and losses usually but not necessarily incurred through default management.

The process of making a temporary suspension or reduction in mortgage payments for a specified period of time. This is usually processed if a hardship is known in advance and proactively discussed with servicer.

The process of accepting payments from borrowers and applying them to the loan financial record. Payments may be applied to interest, principal, fees, late charges, escrow, suspense, homeowner association dues and optional coverage products.
The process of ensuring that investors have received all funds according to the terms of the servicing agreement.
The process of requesting original loan documents from the document custodian and filing applicable lien release(s) with the appropriate recording jurisdiction.

The process of requesting original loan documents from the document custodian in the event of a non-foreclosure liquidation and filing applicable lien release(s) with the appropriate recording jurisdiction.
The process of applying all funds recovered on a loan and removing the outstanding balance from the servicing record.

The process of agreeing to a change in the loan terms or conditions to enable the borrower to retain ownership of the property. Often includes a trial period and some form of underwriting to ensure that the borrower qualifies for the new loan terms.
The process of remitting proceeds received outside of the scheduled reporting cycle according to the terms of the servicing agreement. (i.e. payoff proceeds)

A paper-based process of agreeing to a change in the loan terms or conditions to enable the borrower to retain ownership of the property. Often includes a trial period and some form of underwriting to ensure that the borrower qualifies for the new loan terms.
The process of applying borrower funds to a loan's financial record based on the mortgage note terms and subsequent agreements.

The process of negotiating the property sale, forwarding the sales proceeds to the investor and removing the property from the servicer's accounting ledger. Includes performing a final reconciliation with the investor.
The process in which the Lender requests the Fee Sheet from the Settlement Agent.
An experiment or pilot project, which demonstrates the feasibility of a design concept, business proposal, etc.

changeSet.Term: Proof Of HUD Waiver CAIVRS Clearance
changeSet.Definition: Indicates the review and approval of decision for waiver or resolution of CAIVRS clearance from a HUD representative.
Indicates the borrower's recent debts were not borrowed to meet the cash investment requirement.

changeSet.Term: Proof Of Tax Deferral Or Exemption
changeSet.Definition: Evidence from state or local authority of tax deferral or exemption. An example is a Homestead Exemption Certificate.

Describes the condition of the subject property, or any of a variety of building systems or interior or exterior elements of the structure, or aspects of the surrounding property (such as water or soil).

Describes the information regarding the risk covered by the insurance policy, including the name of the insurance company, its address, name of the policy holder, starting and ending dates of coverage, the actual coverage given in the contract, including locations and amounts.
Explains lenders right to approve a borrower's choice of insurance company and the required specifics of the insurance such as deductible, premium and term. AKA: Agreement to Provide Insurance.

changeSet.Term: Provider Chosen From Lender List Indicator
changeSet.Definition: When true, indicates the borrower chose the service provider from the lender's service providers list.

A cryptographic framework that provides the basis for establishing and maintaining a trustworthy networking environment through the generation and distribution of keys and Digital Certificates. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.

When true, indicates that the property is located within a Planned Unit Development (PUD). A PUD is a project or subdivision that consists of common property and / or improvements that are owned and maintained by an owners’ association for the benefit and use of the individual unit owners.
The process, if allowed by law, where an unsecured money judgement is filed against the borrower because the foreclosure sale funds are insufficient to pay the total debt.
A document that notifies the borrower that the interest rate on the ARM loan has changed.

changeSet.Term: Rate Lock Agreement: Business To Consumer
changeSet.Definition: A written rate lock agreement between a broker or lender and a consumer.
Establishes that the borrower will reinstitute a mortgage debt after bankruptcy proceedings are completed.

The ability of AI systems to identify and classify data, objects, patterns, speech, images, or other inputs. It involves processes such as: 1) Pattern Recognition: Detecting patterns and regularities in data. 2) Image Recognition: Identifying and classifying objects within digital images and videos. 3) Speech Recognition: Interpreting and processing human speech into digital text for further analysis or action.
Time by which services must be resumed to business-critical activities and/or their dependencies and any relevant data recovered and restored.
Documentation showing how the total cost of refinancing was calculated.

Documentation showing how the total cost of refinancing was calculated in accordance with the Anti-Churning Disclosure form to ensure that the mortgagor is not being induced to refinance his/her existing HECM without benefit to the mortgagor and/or solely for the benefit of the mortgagee.

The transaction used to send required information to the MERS eRegistry to report that an eNote has been originated with the MERS eRegistry language. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.

An entity approved by an Issuing Authority to assist Digital Certificate applicants in applying for certificates, and to approve or reject certificate applications, revoke certificates, or renew certificates. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.
The transaction used to reverse an eNote Registration that was registered on the MERS eRegistry. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org

An area of machine learning that focuses on how an intelligent agent should take actions in a dynamic environment to maximize some notion of cumulative reward. It is one of the three basic machine-learning paradigms, along with supervised learning and unsupervised learning. In RL, an agent learns to make decisions by trial and error, interacting with its environment without the need for labeled input/output pairs. The agent’s goal is to find a balance between exploring new actions and exploiting known actions that yield high rewards. This process involves learning a policy that maps states of the environment to the actions that the agent should take.
Organizations are defined as "Related Entities" if: 1. One directly or indirectly controls or is controlled by the other, or 2. One is under direct or indirect common control with the other.
Describes terms and conditions of the relocation package.

Establishes the terms between a relocation company and an employee to purchase a home based on the appraised value. It describes what happens if a home does not sell within a certain period (usually 60 or 90 days), and the circumstances in which a relocation company will buy a home.
Remote notarization of paper documents via audio-video communication platform (Skype, Facetime, etc.)
Remote online notarization of electronic documents with use of multi-factor authentication.

Establishes the rights and duties of the landlord and tenant in a rental transaction. At a minimum identifies the parties, the property, the term of the rental, and the amount of rent for the term. AKA: Lease Agreement.

Evaluates the rental potential of a property and establishes its value. AKA: Operating Income Statement, FHLMC 998, FNMA 216, One to Four Family Investment Property and Two to Four Owner Occupied Property.

An agreement between a servicer and a borrower in which the servicer agrees not to exercise its legal right to foreclose and the borrower agrees to a payment plan that will, over a certain time period, bring the borrower current on the loan.
The process of generating and submitting IRS 1098 forms due to a taxable event to the borrower occurring as a part of the liquidation process.
The process of re-purchasing beneficial or servicing rights from a subsequent servicer or investor due to breach of representations and warranties or loan delinquency.

changeSet.Term: Request For Agreement Of Short Sale
changeSet.Definition: A contract between a buyer and seller (borrower) has been reached and the borrower is requesting approval from the servicer for the short sale prior to the execution of the sales agreement. (Also known as: RASS).

changeSet.Term: Request For Copy Of Tax Return
changeSet.Definition: Authorizes taxing authority (such as IRS) to provide certified copy of borrowers tax return

changeSet.Term: Request For Copy Of Tax Return: IRS 4506
changeSet.Definition: Request for Copy of Tax Return

changeSet.Term: Request For Copy Of Tax Return: IRS 4506TEZ
changeSet.Definition: Short Form Request for Individual Tax Return Transcript. IRS Form 4506T-EZ Rev. January 2012.

Process in which a party, authorized by a taxpayer, submits a paper or electronic request to the IRS for a Tax Return Transcript that is used for Tax Return Verification (TRV). The request includes the signed copy of the IRS Form 4506-C or other form as required by IRS that authorizes the request. The response includes data from the Borrower's tax return.

Process of requesting confirmation from the US Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) of the Borrower's Loan Eligibility and Entitlement for active-duty service members, veterans, reservists, national guard and surviving spouses of veterans.
A worksheet showing the calculation of residual income.
Evidences transactions recorded and account balances for a restricted individual investment account during a specified period.

An artificial intelligence framework for improving the quality of LLM-generated responses by grounding the model on external sources of knowledge to supplement the LLM’s internal representation of information.
Process of ensuring the Closing Protection Letter is on record and covers the loan transaction.

Process of auditing and reconciling the document package data and the loan origination system (LOS) data to ensure the data integrity of the LOS. Provides additional validation that the loan was closed and underwritten correctly.

Process of confirming receipt of the executed closing documents package and performing a review to confirm that all documents are accurately signed and completed, and that all necessary closing conditions were met by the Settlement Agent.
Process of reviewing the real estate tax certification, as provided by the Settlement Agent and/or Title Agent, to confirm taxes required to be collected during the loan closing.
Process of reviewing detailed information from external resources to verify loan data during the loan origination process.
Process of reviewing and verifying the wire instructions are accurate and to ensure that the wired funds will be sent to the correct financial institution and bank account for settlement.

The Residential Standards Governance Committee and the Commercial Standards Governance Committee work in concert with the MISMO Officers and the MISMO Manager and other MISMO committees and report to the MISMO Board of Directors.

Confirms the security interest has been paid off and the lien on the property is released. Required to be recorded. AKA: Reconveyance, Real Estate Lien Release, Satisfaction of Deed of Trust Certificate And Affidavit Of Satisfaction, Certificate Of Discharge, Certificate Of Satisfaction, Deed Of Reconveyance, Deed Of Release, Discharge Of Deed To Secure Debt, Discharge Of Mortgage, Full Deed Of Release, Full Reconveyance, Lost Mortgage Satisfaction, Release Of Lien, Release Of Mortgage, Request For Cancellation, Request For Full [X] / Partial [ ] Release Of Deed Of Trust And Release, Satisfaction, Satisfaction Of Mortgage, Satisfaction Piece, Satisfaction, Cancellation Or Discharge Of Mortgage, Trust Deed Release.
Process of collaborating with all interested parties associated with the transaction to schedule the closing location and closing date and time.
Cryptographic has a function which takes an input and produces a 160-bit hash value known as a message digest, which is typically rendered as a 40-digit hexadecimal number.

The industry-standard method for protecting web communications developed by Netscape Communications Corporation. The SSL security protocol provides data encryption, server authentication, message integrity, and optional client authentication for a TCP-IP connection. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.

The Participant named on the MERS eRegistry that has been sold, pledged, assigned, or granted a security interest in the eNote by the Controller. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.

The Participant that is authorized by the Secured Party to perform certain MERSeRegistry transactions on the Secured Party's behalf. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.
Mortgage or deed of trust evidencing the pledge of real estate as collateral for the loan. Establishes the lender's security interest in the real property.

changeSet.Term: Security Instrument Modification: Consolidation Extension Modification Agreement
changeSet.Definition: Used for refinance loans in state of NY. AKA: CEMA.
Rider that modifies terms of security instrument to provide for assignments to the MERS registry.

When true, indicates that the individual is self-reporting as having served, or is currently serving in the US Armed Forces. Includes enlisted persons that may not have served in “Active Duty” status, and service in the National Guard or Reserves. Also includes “surviving spouses” of Veterans who served and were Missing In Action (MIA) /Killed In Action (KIA), who died of a condition or impairment connected to their service in the Armed Forces (as determined by VA or DoD), or who self-report that their spouse’s service and connected disability/impairment entitles them to benefits from the VA.

changeSet.Term: Seller Lead Hazard Disclosure And Acknowledgment
changeSet.Definition: A document which discloses to buyers known lead-based paint and lead-based paint hazards in the housing and any available reports on lead in the housing.

The process of establishing a relationship with borrowers through written or electronic communication. This may include welcome letters, payment coupons and other information regarding loan activities per RESPA regulations.
Specifies the date and time of the designated Service Event State Type.

Broadly covers the transfers of servicing responsibilities, and in some cases the transfers of servicing rights, in total or in part, through a subservicing or a whole loan servicing arrangement. This transfer of servicing loan data and all historical loan information is transferred from the transferor servicer to the transferee servicer. Impacted parties are notified through items such as goodbye and welcome letters to borrowers. Each servicing transfer is commonly conducted as a one-time event. 'Servicing Transfer' may also be referred to as 'Transfer of Servicing.'
Informs the borrower that the servicing of their loan is being transferred. Required by RESPA / Regulation X. AKA: Notice of Transfer of Servicing, Hello/Goodbye Letter.
The number of minutes spent with an client or borrower in a counseling session.

Describes the funds that are payable at closing. Items that appear on the statement include real estate commissions, loan fees, points, and initial escrow amounts. Required by RESPA/Regulation X. In most cases the Settlement Statement is superseded by the CFPB Closing Disclosure.
The process of establishing a loan record on a servicing system when it is received from an originator (new loan) or another servicer (seasoned loan).
A deed given by court order when a property is sold to satisfy a judgment or tax lien.
An agreement between the investor of a loan and the borrower to enter into a short sale on a property.

An electronic document based on a MISMO specification that locks together a document's data, visual presentation, and signatures such that it detects subsequent tampering and can be programmatically validated to guarantee the original document's integrity. This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.

Confirms that Social Security benefits are payable and the amount received each month. Provided by the Social Security Administration. AKA: Social Security Benefit Letter, Social Security Decision Notice.
Confirms legal ownership of stock in a corporation.

A document issued by the Uniform Collateral Data Portal (UCDP) that summarizes the appraisal submission details, the status of the submission, and the Document File Identifier (Doc File ID) Loans delivered to Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac must have an appraisal with a ""Successful"" status in the UCDP prior to loan delivery.

changeSet.Term: Submit Documentation for VA Full File Loan Review
changeSet.Definition: Process in which the Lender submits required documentation (Loan Review file, UCD and ULAD) for the VA Full File Loan Review (FFLR), using the VA Loan Review API.
Names a successor trustee. AKA: Appointment of Successor Trustee.
