Collects information on borrower homeownership education, housing counseling and language preference to better understand the needs of borrowers during the home buying process.
A formal statement, signed, certified and dated by a surveyor, giving the pertinent facts about a particular property and any easements or encroachments affecting it.

Tamper-Evidencing is a method used in conjunction with Digital Signatures that can determine if a specific section of an Electronic Record has been modified. Evidence of tampering is determined by comparing the Hash Value created for the Digital Signature and a recalculation, at a later time, of the Hash Value from the Electronic Record. See the MISMO XML Digital Signature guide (http://www.mismo.org/files/ImplementationGuidelines/XMLDigitalSignatureI- Guide.pdf).

Targeted area residences are residences located in a census tract in which 70 percent or more of the families have income that is 80 percent or less of the statewide median family income, as defined under Internal Revenue Code Section 143, subsection j, paragraph 2, subparagraph A. The determination that a census tract is a qualified census tract must be based on the most recent decennial census for which data are available, as provided under subsection j, paragraph 2, subparagraph B of the same section. Often called a “targeted area.”

The process of corresponding with interested third parties regarding the servicing administration of a loan. Third parties include but are not limited to mortgage insurers, hazard insurers, optional insurance vendors, tax service companies, homeowners associations (HOA) and attorneys.
A notarial act in which paper documents are notarized in wet ink in the physical presence of the notary.

An Electronic Record under ESIGN and UETA that (1) would be a Promissory Note under the Uniform Commercial Code if the Electronic Record were in writing; (2) the issuer of the Electronic Record expressly has agreed is a Transferable Record; and (3) for purposes of ESIGN, relates to a loan secured by real property. A Transferable Record is also referred to as an eNote. (Refer to Section 16 of UETA and in Title II, Section 201 of E-SIGN.) This term is also defined in the MERS eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.

A mortgage servicer that obtains the rights to service a loan under either a subservicing agreement or an agreement for the sale of mortgage servicing rights (MSR), also referred to as servicing contract rights. The transferee receives the servicing during a servicing transfer.

A mortgage servicer that transfers the rights to service a loan to another servicer via either a subservicing agreement or an agreement for the sale of mortgage servicing rights (MSR), also referred to as servicing contract rights. The transferor releases the servicing during a servicing transfer.
An agreement between a borrower and servicer for a borrower to make payments on a trial basis with the intent to test the borrower's commitment to a proposed permanent modification.

Uniform Electronic Transaction Act. A uniform form of statute that various states have enacted to establish the legal validity and enforceability of electronic signatures, contracts, and other records within the enforcing state. This term is also defined in the MERS® eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.

The Uniform Loan Delivery Dataset (ULDD) is a data format governing loan data delivery and is part of an effort to improve loan quality referred to as the Uniform Mortgage Data Program (UMDP) mandated by the GSEs' regulator, the Federal Home Finance Agency (FHFA).
A telephone, electric or other type of utility bill that shows the name and address.
Used to confirm that the conditions stated in the original appraisal have been met.
Process in which the Lender verifies information that was stated on the loan application.
The employee of a Member who receives all MISMO communications and votes on behalf of the Member on all MISMO matters.

An organization that provides a line of credit (Warehouse Line) to the Lender to fund the loan closing. Funds are repaid when the loan is sold or transferred to a permanent investor. Note: While the loan is in Warehouse, the Warehouse Bank may also act as the Document Custodian.

Work Groups (WGs) and Communities of Practice (COP) conduct MISMOs product development work. Composition, operations, functions, and activities of the WG/COPs are defined in the MISMO Development Process Document (DPD)5: Separate DPDs exist for Residential and Commercial product development. Work Group and Community of Practice participants need not be affiliated with MISMO Members.

Development Process Document Only: As used in this document, "Work Group" refers to all of the volunteer industry working groups that develop MISMO Products including AWG, IM, DWG, COP. NOTE: Contrary to its use throughout the P&Ps, the term Work Group, when used to refer to the Work Group License, encompasses all MISMO groups: the Board, GCs, WGs, and any other subgroups or committees Policies and Procedures Only: As used in the Policies and Procedures, "Work Group" refers to the contributor industry and development work groups that develop MISMO Work Products.
A brief statement describing a DWG's or Community of Practice's purpose and scope.

Extensible Markup Language. XML is a markup language designed specifically for delivering information over the World Wide Web. Defined by the W3C, it is a set of rules for encoding documents in a format that is both human-readable and machine-readable. This term is also defined in the MERS® eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.
A data container within an XML file: <ElementName>Actual Data</ElementName>
